name: stkover
description: A RESERVATION LAID OVER A PARKED TASK, AND THE TASK COMES BACK WHOLE.  When the arena has no free run for a request of kernel.stkover pages or more, Task_AllocStack places it OVER tasks that are not running and can be parked, parks them at the placement (live extent only, to a home image in a swap bank), and the SCHEDULER restores each to its own addresses when it next picks it (Uimg_Ensure).  So: the console shell backgrounds a session shell that sleeps, waits a second for it to settle into wait(), and runs a second session shell -- two of them do not fit the arena side by side, the first is asleep, so the second lands on it and parks it.  The second shell echoes a value it can only have got from its own expansion; the first wakes after the second has exited, is restored, and echoes its own -- a restore that dropped a live byte of the parked shell's frames would not print A=ok.  The klog must carry the placement (stkover), a park (upark) and a restore (urest), and no refusal (upin): the mechanism is observed, not trusted.  The needles are built by expansion, so neither appears in anything typed.
command: tcsh -c 'sleep 3; set a=ok; echo A=$a' & sleep 1; tcsh -c 'set b=ok; echo B=$b'; wait
